subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Gonorrhoea is a sexually transmitted disease caused by a bacterium. How can its spread be controlled?
questions.explain: Gonorrhoea is treated with antibiotics, and barrier methods such as condoms reduce its spread.

questions.q: A new painkiller is tested. In a clinical trial, what is the purpose of giving some patients a placebo?
options: To act as a control so the drug's real effect can be measured
To make the trial finish faster
questions.explain: A placebo acts as a control, allowing scientists to compare and see whether the drug itself has a genuine effect.

questions.q: Alexander Fleming is credited with discovering the first antibiotic, penicillin, which came from:
questions.explain: Fleming discovered that the Penicillium mould produced a substance (penicillin) that killed bacteria.

questions.q: Rose black spot is caused by which type of pathogen?
questions.explain: Rose black spot is a fungal disease that produces purple/black spots on leaves and reduces plant growth.

questions.q: What is the role of fibre in a balanced diet?
options: Helps food move through the gut and prevents constipation
questions.explain: Dietary fibre is not digested but keeps food moving through the intestines.

questions.q: What does protease break protein down into?
questions.explain: Protease enzymes digest proteins into amino acids.

questions.q: Why does emulsifying fat by bile speed up its digestion?
options: It increases the surface area of fat for lipase to act on
Bile chemically digests the fat itself
It absorbs the fat into the blood
questions.explain: Bile breaks large fat droplets into smaller ones, giving lipase a larger surface area to work on.

questions.q: Which food test uses Biuret solution turning from blue to purple?
questions.explain: Biuret solution turns purple/lilac in the presence of protein.

questions.q: Why can viruses NOT be treated with antibiotics?
options: Viruses reproduce inside the body's own cells, where antibiotics cannot easily target them
Viruses are too large for antibiotics to reach
Viruses are killed only by stomach acid
questions.explain: Viruses live and reproduce inside host cells, so antibiotics (which target bacterial processes) cannot kill them.

questions.q: A vaccine usually contains:
options: Dead or inactive forms of a pathogen (or its antigens)
questions.explain: Vaccines contain dead or inactivated pathogens that trigger an immune response without causing disease.

questions.q: Which nutrient is mainly needed for growth and repair of tissues?
questions.explain: Proteins provide the amino acids needed to build and repair body tissues.

questions.q: Which nutrient is the body's main source of energy?
questions.explain: Carbohydrates are the primary energy source in a balanced diet.

questions.q: What happens to a digestive enzyme if the pH is far from its optimum?
options: It turns into a different enzyme
Its active site changes shape (denatures) and it stops working
questions.explain: Extremes of pH denature an enzyme by changing the shape of its active site so the substrate no longer fits.

questions.q: Which of these is a NON-specific first line of defence against pathogens?
options: The skin acting as a barrier
questions.explain: The skin is a physical barrier that is non-specific, stopping pathogens entering before the immune response.

questions.q: Where is most digested food absorbed into the blood?
questions.explain: The small intestine is adapted with villi to absorb digested food molecules.

questions.q: Which type of enzyme are amylase and other carbohydrases?
questions.explain: Enzymes are proteins that act as biological catalysts.

questions.q: Which organ produces amylase, protease and lipase?
questions.explain: The pancreas makes all three types of digestive enzyme and releases them into the small intestine.

questions.q: Which disease is caused by a protist spread by mosquitoes?
questions.explain: Malaria is caused by a protist, with mosquitoes acting as vectors that transfer it between people.

questions.q: During which stage are new drugs first tested for toxicity on cells, tissues and live animals?
questions.explain: Preclinical testing uses cells, tissues and animals before any human trials begin.

questions.q: HIV is best described as a pathogen that is a:
options: Virus that attacks white blood cells (lymphocytes)
Bacterium that lives in the gut
questions.explain: HIV is a virus that attacks and destroys lymphocytes, eventually leading to AIDS if untreated.

questions.q: Salmonella food poisoning is caused by:
options: Bacteria spread in unhygienically prepared food
questions.explain: Salmonella bacteria are spread in food prepared in unhygienic conditions and produce toxins.

questions.q: A balanced diet should contain water, fibre and which group of main nutrients?
options: Carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, vitamins and minerals
questions.explain: A balanced diet supplies carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, vitamins, minerals, water and fibre.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Biology (2017) specification; Nutrition Health
